# visionary_api_key (Resource)

An API key. Visionary shows the key once, when it is made, so it is kept in the state as secret; keys can't be changed, so any change makes a new key and revokes the old one. Needs an admin key.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A server key for an SDK, handed to another module or a secret store.
resource "visionary_api_key" "checkout_sdk" {
  name  = "checkout service"
  scope = "server"
}

output "checkout_sdk_key" {
  value     = visionary_api_key.checkout_sdk.secret
  sensitive = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Name.
- `scope` (String) read (the HTTP API as a viewer), editor or admin (the HTTP API with that role), server (SDKs, OTLP, the host agent), client (browsers and apps) or scim.

### Optional

- `expires_days` (Number) Days until it expires; leave out for never.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) When it was made.
- `expires_at` (String) When it expires, if it does.
- `id` (String) The id Visionary gave it.
- `prefix` (String) The visible start of the key.
- `secret` (String, Sensitive) The key, vis_…. Empty for an imported key.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The id is the number Visionary shows. An imported key's secret stays
# empty: Visionary only shows it when the key is made.
terraform import visionary_api_key.example 12
```
